speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, weight, or bowel habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your age and the presence of a large ovarian mass causing shortness of breath and abdominal distension, have you noticed any changes in your urinary frequency or feelings of pelvic pressure?

REQUEST TEST: Tumor_Marker_Panels (CA-125, HE4, CEA, CA19-9).
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound, Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The tumor marker panel results show a normal CA-125 level, which is an important clue given your symptoms. While a normal CA-125 does not rule out ovarian pathology, it makes epithelial ovarian cancer less likely. Have you noticed any pain in your lower back, legs, or swelling in your extremities?

REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_MRI.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Fibroma (Meigs Syndrome).

The combination of a large ovarian mass, ascites (increased abdominal girth), and pleural effusion (shortness of breath) with normal CA-125 and no weight loss strongly points to Meigs syndrome rather than malignancy.
